Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Nyrstar temporarily suspended production at its Middle Tennessee zinc mines in late November 2023; The suspension was due to decreasing zinc prices; The suspension was due to the impact of inflation on input costs <2> The International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) met in October; ILZSG revised its 2023 forecast; the 2023 forecast was revised from a deficit of 45,000 tonnes <3> A market analysis report on the global zinc market was published, which includes a historical data review for the period of 2019-2023 and a forecast for 2024-2029. [1, 2] The report projects that the market size will increase by USD 4.46 billion between 2024 and 2029, growing at a CAGR of 2.8%. [1] Key drivers for this growth include rapid industrialization in emerging economies, infrastructure development, and growth in the automotive industry. [2, 3] The analysis covers various market segments, including application (industrial, human health), end-user (construction, transportation), and geography (APAC, North America, Europe, etc.). [3, 4] <4> FocusEconomics reported that zinc prices averaged USD 2,763 per metric ton in July; a 4.1% increase from June; The report attributed the rise to US trade deals with the EU and several Asian countries, which eased fears of a trade war that could impact zinc demand <5> A strike was initiated at Newmont's Peñasquito mine in Mexico; The strike began on June 7, 2023; The strike led to a suspension of operations <6> In the first quarter of 2023, the United States Mint produced a total of 3,442,560,000 circulating coins. The production was split between the Denver Mint, which struck 1,822,080,000 coins, and the Philadelphia Mint, which made 1,620,480,000 coins. A significant portion of this production, approximately 38.1% or 1,312.4 million coins, consisted of Lincoln cents. Given that Lincoln cents are composed of copper-plated zinc, this level of production highlights a consistent demand for zinc from this sector.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The price of zinc reached its yearly high of $3,198 per metric ton on October 2, 2024. Throughout the fourth quarter of 2024, the price largely remained above $3,000, though it experienced some volatility. It briefly dropped below this threshold on November 8 but recovered by November 25, ultimately ending the year at $2,978.50 on December 31. <2> A retrospective analysis of the second half of 2024 revealed significant volatility in zinc prices. Beginning H2 at US$2,928.50, the price declined through July, hitting a low for the half at US$2,581.50 on August 7. Subsequently, the price experienced notable fluctuations, peaking at US$2,943 on August 27, then dipping to US$2,712 on September 10. Following this, the price rebounded, reaching a yearly high of US$3,198 on October 2. <3> A market analysis of the London Metal Exchange (LME) confirms that High-Grade zinc prices decreased by 3.64% during the fourth quarter of 2024. [4] Despite the quarterly drop, the metal had a strong annual performance, with prices moving 12.06% higher for the full year. [4] The settlement price for three-month LME zinc forwards at the end of 2024 was $2,978.50 per ton. [9] Another analysis reported a similar full-year gain of 13%, with the price rising from $2,621 to $2,979 per metric ton. [5, 7] Raw data for the LME Zinc Cash-Settlement price on the final day of trading was $2,974.00. [6] <4> According to the United States Mint's 2024 Annual Report, the total cost to produce and circulate a one-cent coin (penny) during Fiscal Year 2024 was 3.69 cents, a significant increase from the 3.07 cents reported in FY2023. [1, 6, 9] For the 19th consecutive year, the production cost for a penny has exceeded its face value. [1, 4, 6] The cost is influenced by the market prices of its component metals (the penny's composition is a copper-plated zinc core), as well as manufacturing, distribution, and administrative expenses. [6, 9] The reported loss, or negative seigniorage, for the penny in FY2024 amounted to $85.3 million. [7, 9] The data covers the fiscal year ending September 30, 2024, and the official report was published by the U.S. Mint on December 9, 2024. [6, 9] <5> According to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), the monthly average North American price for Special High Grade (SHG) zinc in September 2024 was 146.93 cents per pound, which was a 4% increase compared to August 2024. Domestic recoverable mine production for September 2024 was 57,000 metric tons. The average daily mine production was 1,900 tons, a 9% decrease from the previous month. The USGS publishes this data retrospectively; the report for September 2024 was officially published in December 2024. <6> In an article published on October 23, 2024, it was reported that the global zinc market forecast for 2024 has shifted from an anticipated supply surplus of 56,000 metric tons to a significant deficit of 164,000 tons. This change is attributed to a number of factors, including falling mine production for the third consecutive year. While demand growth in China, a major consumer, is expected to slow from 7.4% in 2023 to 1.4% in 2024, demand is projected to rise in the United States, Turkey, India, Italy, and Japan. <7> The International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) updated its forecast; indicating a global zinc supply deficit of 164,000 metric tons for 2024; This is a significant revision from their previous forecast of a 56,000-ton surplus <8> In a revised forecast announced in early October 2024, the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) projected that the global refined zinc market would experience a 164,000 metric ton deficit in 2024. [7, 8] This marks a significant reversal from its April 2024 forecast, which had anticipated a surplus of 56,000 tons. [7] The updated outlook is attributed to reduced output in several regions, including Europe. [7] The forecast also anticipates a decline in zinc mine production in the United States, among other countries like China, Canada, South Africa, and Peru. [7] <9> By the end of June 2024, zinc ingot prices in the USA increased, driven by a combination of supply chain disruptions and robust demand. The ongoing logistical issues reduced the availability of zinc ingots and created bottlenecks, putting upward pressure on prices. On the demand side, consumption was strong, bolstered by increased activity in the construction sector. Furthermore, the automobile industry saw a significant 25% increase in sales volume in June compared to May, boosting demand for zinc, which is a critical component for galvanization and corrosion resistance in vehicle manufacturing. <10> An analyst from ChemAnalyst has predicted that zinc ingot prices in the USA are likely to increase, a forecast published on July 8, 2024. This projection is attributed to rising demand from various downstream sectors. A potential resurgence in the construction industry is highlighted as a key factor that could stimulate buying activity and contribute to the price hike.

metadata.original_text: This time series records zinc USD T data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-10-06 to 2025-10-21. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In early September 2025, zinc futures experienced a significant rally, climbing above $2,890 per tonne to their highest level since March 28 of that year. [5] The price increase was part of a broader rally across base metals. [5] This surge was supported by a weaker US dollar and growing market expectations that the US Federal Reserve would implement an interest rate cut in its upcoming September meeting, a move anticipated to improve credit conditions. [5] The rally was in anticipation of a future cut rather than an actual rate cut, and the peak reached remained below the $3000 per tonne mark. [5] <2> The White House issued an executive order; that modified the scope of reciprocal tariffs.; This included adding certain critical minerals to a list of exempted goods <3> A report issued on September 2, 2025, confirmed that U.S. manufacturing operating conditions in August 2025 improved at the strongest rate in over three years. The final S&P Global US Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) registered 53.0, a significant increase from 49.8 in July and the highest reading since May 2022. This figure was slightly revised down from a preliminary 'flash' estimate of 53.3. The surge was underpinned by the steepest rise in production since May 2022 and an eighth consecutive month of growth in new orders. A key driver of the upturn was significant inventory building, with finished goods stocks rising at the fastest pace in over a year. This stockpiling was linked to manufacturers' concerns about future price increases and potential supply chain constraints due to tariffs. These tariff concerns also contributed to a steep rise in input costs, leading to a sharp increase in selling prices. In response to increased orders and capacity pressures, factories also increased their staffing levels. <4> A retrospective market analysis for July 2025 indicated that U.S. zinc oxide prices declined due to surplus imports and varied demand across sectors. [1] The market was kept well-stocked by reliable import streams from Canada and Mexico. [1] Demand trends diverged by industry; while the automotive sector saw an 8.9% month-on-month increase in vehicle sales, boosting zinc oxide consumption in tire and rubber manufacturing, the construction sector's demand remained weak, subdued by high interest rates and affordability pressures. [1] <5> On August 5, 2025, the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis jointly announced that the international trade deficit in goods and services for June 2025 was $60.2 billion, a decrease from a revised $71.7 billion in May. [1, 3, 4] Total exports for June were $277.3 billion, and imports were $337.5 billion. [1, 3] According to detailed commodity data, U.S. exports of 'Zinc Powder' in June 2025 totaled $2.57 million, while imports amounted to $6.16 million, creating a negative trade balance of $3.58 million for that specific category. [6] <6> The price of zinc reached a year-to-date high of US$2,971 per metric ton on March 14, 2025. This peak occurred after the metal gained support throughout February and March, including a climb to US$2,928 on February 24, 2025. The news of this market activity was reported on August 1, 2025. <7> Throughout July 2025, the U.S. zinc market faced volatility influenced by a combination of factors, including a supply surplus, weak demand, and changing U.S. trade policies. An oversupply in the market was indicated by a sharp increase in smelter fees and a consecutive build-up of inventory. Demand from the construction sector, a primary user of zinc for galvanized steel, was weak due to seasonal slowdowns and the lingering impact of high inflation and interest rates. Furthermore, uncertainty regarding potential U.S. tariffs on imports created cautious sentiment among investors. Despite these pressures, the zinc price experienced some fluctuation, peaking at US$2,865 on July 23. <8> The price of zinc demonstrated significant volatility throughout the first half of 2025. The year began with a downward trend, as the price per metric ton fell from US$3,150 on December 10 to US$2,750 by January 31. A recovery in the following months led to a year-to-date high of US$2,971 on March 14. However, this was followed by a sharp decline to a year-to-date low of US$2,562 on April 9. The market remained volatile, with a subsequent peak on July 23 reaching US$2,865, a level below the highs observed in the first quarter. <9> A market review of the first half of 2025 reported that the price of zinc climbed to US$2,928 per metric ton on February 24, 2025, as part of a temporary recovery in February and March. [3] However, data from the London Metal Exchange (LME) shows the official cash settlement price for zinc on that day was US$2,840.00 per metric ton. [2, 7] The broader context for the first half of the year included price volatility influenced by a supply surplus, weak demand from the construction sector, and changing US trade policies. [3, 4] After the February recovery, the zinc price hit a year-to-date high in March before falling to a low point in April 2025. [3] <10> The global zinc market is experiencing significant volatility driven by escalating international trade tensions and the issuance of new tariff letters to eight countries. The United States is a key player in these ongoing discussions. Concurrently, the European Union is intensively working towards reaching a comprehensive trade agreement with the U.S. by a target date of August 1, 2025. Additionally, high-level economic talks between the US Commerce Secretary and Chinese officials are anticipated in early August.

metadata.original_text: This time series records zinc USD T data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-12-31 to 2026-01-16. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On December 16, 2025, Morgan Stanley revised its global zinc price outlook for 2026, projecting an annual average of $2,900 per metric ton. The slightly lowered forecast reflects expectations of a broader market surplus through 2026, driven by recovering inventories on the London Metal Exchange, increased Chinese exports, and anticipated growth in global mine supply. <2> Argus Media reported that negotiations for 2026 long-term zinc contracts in the US market experienced significant slowdowns, with many contracts remaining incomplete ahead of a late-November 2025 deadline. This delay was primarily driven by severe backwardation creating psychological barriers and a steep 75 percent decline in London Metal Exchange (LME) registered warehouse stocks, which fell from approximately 175,000 tonnes at the start of 2025 to just 43,750 tonnes by November. <3> ChemAnalyst reported that US zinc oxide prices increased by 3% in October 2025 due to tight supply conditions and steady downstream demand from the automotive and tire sectors. <4> The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI increased to 52.5 in October 2025, an increase from 52.0 in the preceding month. This reading, which was slightly above the preliminary estimate of 52.2, indicated the third consecutive month of expansion in the manufacturing sector. The growth was underpinned by an accelerated rate of output and the most significant rise in new orders in 20 months, attributed to stronger market demand and success in securing new contracts. However, this expansion was primarily driven by domestic demand, as new export orders declined for the fourth successive month. <5> On October 20, 2025, Titan Mining Corporation announced the discovery of significant concentrations of Germanium at its wholly-owned Empire State Mine in St. Lawrence County, New York. The Germanium, a U.S.-designated critical mineral, was identified within the mine's existing zinc-processing circuit, which means no new mining is required to access it. Initial sampling showed the plant feed graded 21 g/t Germanium, which was enriched to 77 g/t in the pre-float stream. This discovery is considered a major development that could add a valuable by-product to Titan's zinc operations, enhancing the mine's economics with minimal additional capital requirements. CEO Rita Adiani stated that the discovery represents an "exciting new value driver for Titan and a strategic asset for the United States," which could help create a more resilient domestic supply chain for the critical mineral. The company has completed an initial plant survey and is moving forward with daily sampling and a test program to establish a cost-effective recovery process. <6> In early September 2025, zinc futures experienced a significant rally, climbing above $2,890 per tonne to their highest level since March 28 of that year. [5] The price increase was part of a broader rally across base metals. [5] This surge was supported by a weaker US dollar and growing market expectations that the US Federal Reserve would implement an interest rate cut in its upcoming September meeting, a move anticipated to improve credit conditions. [5] The rally was in anticipation of a future cut rather than an actual rate cut, and the peak reached remained below the $3000 per tonne mark. [5] <7> The White House issued an executive order; that modified the scope of reciprocal tariffs.; This included adding certain critical minerals to a list of exempted goods <8> A report issued on September 2, 2025, confirmed that U.S. manufacturing operating conditions in August 2025 improved at the strongest rate in over three years. The final S&P Global US Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) registered 53.0, a significant increase from 49.8 in July and the highest reading since May 2022. This figure was slightly revised down from a preliminary 'flash' estimate of 53.3. The surge was underpinned by the steepest rise in production since May 2022 and an eighth consecutive month of growth in new orders. A key driver of the upturn was significant inventory building, with finished goods stocks rising at the fastest pace in over a year. This stockpiling was linked to manufacturers' concerns about future price increases and potential supply chain constraints due to tariffs. These tariff concerns also contributed to a steep rise in input costs, leading to a sharp increase in selling prices. In response to increased orders and capacity pressures, factories also increased their staffing levels.
